title.en: Clothing Ontology for Outfit Combination Engine

description.en: An OWL 2 ontology that models clothing items, their attributes (color, material, size, formality), and outfit-level compatibility relations. The ontology is designed to support a rule-based outfit combination engine that recommends harmonious outfits based on color theory, material compatibility, occasion, season, and personalized user preferences.

comments.en: Version 2 extends v1 with: an Outfit module (Outfit class and part-of properties), a richer Attribute module (ColorScheme, ColorUndertone, FormalityLevel), a User module for personalization, schema.org alignment, and one machine-readable SWRL rule plus documented rule designs for color-harmony, formality-consistency, season-coherence and material-conflict heuristics.

Loose-fitting Top, typically SmartCasual to BusinessCasual.
Outfit whose items each have FormalDress formality. Target class for documented SWRL rule R2; only R1 is machine-encoded in this version.
Head Accessory.

Named aesthetic style preference (Minimalist, Classic, Streetwear, BohoChic, Sporty, ...).
Abstract grouping class for properties used to describe a ClothingItem (Color, Material, Size, Season, Occasion, Gender, FormalityLevel, ColorScheme, ColorUndertone).
Dress-code level: Casual, SmartCasual, BusinessCasual, FormalDress.
Neck Accessory.
Wrist Accessory.
Example casual summer combination demonstrating the engine's expected output.

A complete styled combination of clothing items containing at least a Top, a Bottom and Footwear, optionally extended with Outerwear and Accessories. Outfits are the primary output of the recommendation engine.
Foot covering (Boots, Sandals, FormalShoes, SportsShoes).
A color-theory scheme applied to an Outfit (Monochromatic, Analogous, Complementary, Triadic, Neutral).
Non-garment wearable that complements an outfit (Belt, Hat, Scarf, Watch).
Knitted Top suitable for cold seasons.
Body-shape classification used by future fit-aware recommendations.
A textile material or fabric (Cotton, Wool, Silk, Polyester, ...).
Ankle-or-higher Footwear, typically Autumn/Winter.
Long Outerwear designed for cold weather.
A season of the year (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter).
Denim Bottom; Casual to SmartCasual.
Athletic Footwear (sneaker, running shoe).
Lower-body garment (Jean, Trouser, Short, Skirt).
Tailored Bottom; BusinessCasual to FormalDress.
A social occasion or context (Casual, Work, Formal, Sport).
A standard garment size (XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL).
Short-sleeved knit Top, typically Casual.
FormalDress-level Footwear (oxford, derby, loafer).
End user of the outfit recommendation engine. Owns clothing items, has stated preferences, and receives recommended Outfits.
Undertone classification of a Color: Warm, Cool, or NeutralUndertone.
Top-level class for any wearable article. Direct subclasses partition garments by body region (Top, Bottom, Outerwear, Footwear, Accessory).
An Outfit whose constituent items satisfy the color-harmony and formality-consistency rules. Membership is inferred by the SWRL ruleset.
Knee-length or shorter Bottom; Casual, Summer-leaning.
A named color value (Red, Blue, Black, ...).
Associates a clothing item with a single size value drawn from a standard size scale.
Symmetric compatibility relation between two clothing items, inferred by the SWRL outfit-compatibility rules.
Retail price of the clothing item, expressed as a decimal value. Currency is not encoded at the property level.
Relates an Outfit to the Top garment it contains.
Relates an Outfit to the Bottom garment it contains.
Relates an Outfit to the Top garment it contains.
The overall color scheme of an outfit (e.g., Monochromatic, Complementary, Analogous).
Optional accessory(ies) included in an Outfit (belt, hat, watch, scarf).
Relates an Outfit to its footwear component.
Indicates that the clothing item is designed or commonly worn for a given gender presentation. Use :Unisex when no preference applies.
Body type of the user, used by future fit-aware recommendations.
Associates a clothing item with one or more colors that appear on it.
Outfit that the engine has produced as a recommendation for the user.
Boolean flag stating whether the item can be machine-washed.
Symmetric relation between two colors that form an aesthetically pleasing pair according to color-theory heuristics (complementary, analogous, neutral pairing).
The dress-code formality level of a clothing item (Casual, SmartCasual, BusinessCasual, FormalDress).
Free-text brand or manufacturer name of the clothing item.
States that a clothing item or an outfit is suitable for a particular season. The domain is the union of ClothingItem and Outfit because both individual garments and whole outfits carry a season.
Relates an Outfit to its footwear component.
Associates a clothing item with its primary fabric or material composition.
The undertone (warm, cool, or neutral) of a color. Used by the color harmony rules of the outfit engine.
Relates an Outfit to the Bottom garment it contains.
Specialization of colorHarmonizesWith for the complementary case (opposite hues on the color wheel).
Records a style category the user reports as a preference (Minimalist, Classic, Streetwear, etc.).
Optional outerwear component of an Outfit (jacket, coat, etc.).
Display name of the user.

States that a clothing item or an outfit is suitable for a particular social occasion. The domain is the union of ClothingItem and Outfit because both individual garments and whole outfits carry an occasion.
Records a color the user reports as a preference. Used by the personalization layer when ranking recommended outfits.
Age of the user in completed years.
Associates a user with the clothing items currently in their wardrobe.
Symmetric incompatibility relation between two clothing items (e.g., conflicting formality or clashing colors).
